objective: Operationalize the attached every-run autonomous improvement loop with research, baseline, isolated candidate, validation, measured promotion, explicit rollback, and fail-closed authority boundaries.

requirement_families: current open-source and commercial ecosystem research
reasoning, planning, decomposition, reflection, verification, and long-horizon execution
autonomous coding, sandboxing, testing, checkpoints, rollback, and recovery
self-improvement candidate isolation, benchmark, comparison, promotion, and rollback
reliability, adversarial checking, security, graceful failure, and performance
AGI-oriented generalization and continuous knowledge acquisition without unsupported AGI claims
attachment.implementation_decision: Existing FAISAL subsystems cover most capability families; the missing cross-cutting mechanism was a durable evidence-bound improvement candidate lifecycle.

research.conclusion: Agents plan, call tools, collaborate across specialists, maintain state, use handoffs, guardrails, approvals, tracing, sessions, and resumable results.
research.implementation_impact: Evolution candidates require explicit isolation, validation, approval evidence when configured, promotion, and rollback rather than trusting model-generated upgrade proposals.

research.conclusion: MCP standardizes resources, prompts, tools, capability negotiation, asynchronous Tasks, progress/cancellation, and explicit consent/tool-safety guidance; tool descriptions and annotations are untrusted unless obtained from a trusted server.
research.implementation_impact: Research, MCP metadata, tool descriptions, and model outputs are recorded as digests/data and never become promotion authority.

research.conclusion: Current vLLM supports continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, speculative decoding, multimodal processing, tool/reasoning parsers, fault tolerance, and broad hardware integrations.
research.implementation_impact: Provider-specific runtime improvements remain user-space candidates and must pass the same evidence/promotion/rollback transaction.

research.conclusion: Durable checkpointers support short-term thread recovery while stores support long-term cross-thread memory; retention and production persistence require explicit policy.
research.implementation_impact: The evolution journal binds improvement evidence and rollback state separately from execution snapshots and long-term memory.

implementation.state_machine: DRAFT -> ISOLATED -> VALIDATED -> PROMOTED; VALIDATED -> REJECTED; PROMOTED -> ROLLED_BACK
features: baseline and candidate artifact digest binding
minimum improvement and maximum regression policy
SHA-256 journal continuity and replay verification

validation.selftest: FEV_EVOLUTION_SELFTEST_OK cases=29 promoted=1 rolled_back=1 rejected=2 replay=verified model_authority=denied

benchmark.interpretation: The full lifecycle is intentionally slower than raw metric comparison because it performs durable journal writes, SHA-256 digests, policy checks, approval gating, and receipts. This is control-plane safety overhead, not an end-to-end AI performance claim.

live_model_catalog.interpretation: The catalog was researched for provider-neutral ecosystem analysis only. No model output, model ID, price, or provider metadata grants authority.

qualification_limits: The evolution transaction governs bounded evidence and release decisions; it does not autonomously edit privileged kernel code or deploy software.
The benchmark measures control-plane durability and policy overhead, not inference quality, tokens/sec, general intelligence, or overall system productivity.
No live paid-model call, MCP server, browser session, robotics device, physical accelerator, production cluster, or independent operator approval ceremony was used.

Skill extraction, meta-learning, model routing, memory, browser, multimodal, and robotics capabilities remain implemented in their existing provider-neutral subsystems; this iteration supplies the missing cross-cutting improvement-governance transaction rather than claiming all ecosystems are equivalent.
Production approval remains blocked by the established independent builder, signing, physical hardware, secure boot/TPM, live multihost, independent security review, and CVE-ownership requirements.
